name: Hooga ULTRA360
short_review: The most fully specified compact panel in this round-up. Every one of its 72 LEDs carries four chips (630, 660, 810 and 850 nm), and Hooga publishes a full irradiance-by-distance table rather than a single headline number. Touchscreen controls let you set red and near-infrared brightness separately, plus a 1–30 minute timer and pulse mode. It sits on a tabletop stand and is sized for face, neck, shoulders and joints rather than whole-body sessions. It leads this list on published specs, its three-year warranty and a solid Amazon.co.uk review base (4.6★ from 182 ratings on 9 Nov 2026).

specs.Controls: Touchscreen, independent red/NIR brightness, 1–30 min timer, pulse

pros: Independent red and NIR brightness control
cons: Targeted size, not a full-body panel
Tabletop use only; will not attach to Hooga mobile stands

name: Nebula NB600 600W Red Light Therapy Panel
short_review: If you want more than a face-and-shoulders panel, this is the bigger option here from a UK company (Vipertech Ltd, Peterborough). At 62 × 21 cm with 120 dual-chip LEDs it covers a much taller area in one session, and separate red and NIR switches let you run either or both. Nebula's UK manual quotes above 101 mW/cm² at 6" and 67 mW/cm² at 12". The trade-off: owner reviews on Nebula's own site point out there is no built-in timer, so you will need a plug timer or a phone alarm.

name: Inthered ITR-EVO 300W
short_review: A newer UK-supported brand that focuses on proof. Inthered says its >156 mW/cm² figure is measured at the panel surface and checked by an independent third party, and it publishes a safety and quality report. In practice you get 60 dual-chip LEDs behind 30° lenses, an aluminium body, touchscreen modes (red, NIR or both), four brightness steps, 10/20/40 Hz pulse and a 5–30 minute auto-off timer. It ranks mid-table only because it is new: four Amazon.co.uk ratings on 9 Nov 2026.
